name: Visitor without permission for paid activities (no visa needed)
summary: Citizens of countries on the INM no-visa list, plus anyone holding a valid visa from Canada, Japan, the US, the UK or a Schengen country, can visit for under 180 days without a Mexican visa. No paid work.

other: Passport from a country on the INM visa-exempt list (check the official list), or a valid visa from Canada, Japan, the US, the UK or a Schengen country, or permanent residence in Spain, a Schengen country, the US, Canada, Japan, the UK or Pacific Alliance members (Chile, Colombia, Peru). Spanish cards must say PERMANENTE or LARGA DURACION.
Allowed: tourism, transit, unpaid business meetings, religious, press, artistic or sports activities, medical treatment, short studies.
The exact exempt-country list was not readable in full on the pages opened, and the facilitation page was last updated Jan 2024, so confirm the current list.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Barcelona: entry without a visa
Mexican embassy: travel facilitation
DOF: Lineamientos generales para la expedicion de visas

stay.note: Immigration sets the days at the border. It can never be more than 180.

processing: Entry is decided by immigration officers at the port of entry. A visa or exemption does not guarantee entry.

name: Visitor Visa without Permission for Paid Activities
summary: Visa for visits up to 180 days with no paid work, for nationals who need one. Apply at a Mexican embassy or consulate and book through MiConsulado.

other: Show ties to your home country, economic solvency, an invitation from an organization, or another listed reason (humanitarian, research, studies, an official event).

sources.label: Mexican consulate Peten: visitor visa without paid activities

documents: Proof of legal stay if you apply outside your country of nationality
Proof of ties, solvency, invitation or other listed basis
steps: Attend at the consulate with your documents
Border officers make the final entry decision

name: Electronic Visa (visitor, by air)
summary: Online visa for nationals Mexico allows to apply electronically, for people flying in as visitors without paid work. Valid 180 days from issue, one entry.

other: Only for nationalities Mexico authorizes. The country list was not published on the pages opened.
Must travel by air.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Presidio: electronic visa
DOF: Lineamientos generales para la expedicion de visas

steps: Upload a face photo and passport data page

name: Transit through Mexico
summary: Transit to a third country counts as a permitted visitor activity under the same rules as visa-free or visa entry. Airside transit rules were not found on the official pages opened.

other: Same visa rules as visitors. Airside transit visa rules not confirmed, check with the nearest Mexican consulate.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Barcelona: entry without a visa

name: Temporary Resident Visa (economic solvency)
summary: Visa for stays over 180 days and up to 4 years if you prove income or savings. Thresholds are set in days of the Mexico City minimum wage. Figures below are from the Houston consulate.

income.note: 300 days of the Mexico City general minimum wage, after taxes, for each of the last 6 months. Approx figure quoted by the Houston consulate.

savings.note: 5,000 days of the Mexico City minimum wage, month-end balance for each of the last 12 months. Approx figure quoted by the Houston consulate.

other: Meet either the income test or the savings test.
Add 100 days of minimum wage (about USD 1,464.70) per dependent for the savings test.
Other consulates may quote different USD conversions.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Houston: temporary resident visa, financial solvency
Mexican consulate Houston: temporary resident visa (180 days to 4 years)

stay.note: More than 180 days, up to 4 years.

documents: 12 months of bank statements, or 6 months of pay or pension proof
steps: After entering Mexico, get your residence card from INM within 30 days
processing: Issuance depends on a consular interview.

name: Temporary Resident Visa (job offer)
summary: Work in Mexico on a temporary resident visa. If your salary is paid in Mexico, the employer must first get INM authorization. Details were not fully readable.

other: Employer must get INM authorization if paid in Mexico. The dedicated job-offer consulate page was unreachable, so process details need review.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Houston: temporary resident visa (180 days to 4 years)

stay.note: Up to 4 years for the temporary resident visa.

name: Temporary Resident Visa (family unit)
summary: Temporary resident visa on the family unit basis. Listed by the consulate. Detailed requirements were not on the page opened.

other: Requirements for family unit were not detailed on the page opened.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Houston: temporary resident visa (180 days to 4 years)

name: Temporary Resident Visa (property or investor)
summary: The consulate lists owning real estate in Mexico or being an investor as bases for a temporary resident visa. Amounts were not published on the pages opened.

other: Property and investor thresholds not found on the pages opened. Check with the consulate.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Houston: temporary resident visa (180 days to 4 years)

name: Temporary Resident Student Visa
summary: Visa to study in Mexico. Students can ask INM for permission to do paid work.

other: Proof of studies or an international mobility instrument.
Solvency from you, a parent or guardian (if 25 or younger), a school scholarship letter, or a bank document.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Presidio: temporary resident student visa

steps: Get your residence card from INM within 30 days of entering

name: Permanent Resident Visa (pension or retirement)
summary: Permanent residence for people over 64 with a pension or large savings. Figures are from the Houston consulate.

income.note: 500 days of the Mexico City minimum wage, after taxes, for each of the last 6 months. Approx figure from Houston consulate.

savings.note: 20,000 days of the Mexico City minimum wage, month-end balance for each of the last 12 months. Approx figure from Houston consulate.

other: Page says over 64 years old. Meet either the pension or the savings test.

sources.label: Mexican consulate Houston: permanent resident visa, pension or retirement

documents: Pension letter plus 6 months of proof, or 12 months of bank statements
Proof of legal status if not a US citizen

name: Permanent Resident Visa (general)
summary: Consulates issue a permanent resident visa for moving to Mexico indefinitely. The El Paso page lists documents only and no thresholds. Other routes (family, points) were not confirmed.

other: No income thresholds on the page opened. Not authorized to work on this visa as described by El Paso consulate.

sources.label: Mexican consulate El Paso: permanent resident visa

name: Naturalization by Residence
summary: Mexican citizenship after 5 years of residence with a temporary or permanent resident card. Student residence does not count.

eligibility.language: Spanish exam plus Mexican history and culture exam
other: Residence card must be valid 6 months after filing.
Clean federal and local criminal records.
Fee not shown on the page opened. Dual citizenship not stated on this page.
Pass exams showing you speak Spanish, know Mexican history and are integrated into the culture (refugees, minors and people over 60 only take the Spanish exam).

sources.label: SRE: naturalization by residence
Mexican consulate UK: Mexican nationality

citizenship.note: Naturalized Mexicans can lose nationality by voluntarily acquiring another one or using a foreign passport, per the consulate page. Confirm before applying.

name: Naturalization by Marriage to a Mexican
summary: Citizenship after 2 years of marriage and 2 years of residence in Mexico with a residence card.

other: Marriage at least 2 years old.
Residence card valid 6 months after filing.
Spouse signs a statement that the marriage continues.
Pass exams showing you speak Spanish, know Mexican history and are integrated into the culture (refugees, minors and people over 60 only take the Spanish exam).

name: Naturalization (Latin American or Iberian origin)
summary: Shorter path for people from a Latin American country or the Iberian peninsula: 2 years of residence.

other: Qualifying country list not shown on the page opened.
Pass exams showing you speak Spanish, know Mexican history and are integrated into the culture (refugees, minors and people over 60 only take the Spanish exam).

sources.label: SRE: naturalization for Latin American or Iberian origin

name: Naturalization (parent of Mexican-born child)
summary: Parents of children Mexican by birth can naturalize after 2 years of residence.

other: Pass exams showing you speak Spanish, know Mexican history and are integrated into the culture (refugees, minors and people over 60 only take the Spanish exam).

sources.label: SRE: naturalization for parents of Mexican-born children

name: Mexican nationality by birth or descent
summary: Anyone born in Mexico is Mexican, whatever the parents' nationality. Children born abroad to a Mexican parent (including a naturalized one) are Mexican by birth. The page sets no generation limit.

other: Mexicans by birth can hold another nationality and must identify as Mexican when entering or leaving.

sources.label: Mexican consulate UK: Mexican nationality

citizenship.note: Dual is fine for Mexicans by birth. Naturalized citizens can lose nationality by voluntarily taking another.
